# The WithAll query scope and its filters

> A Sequelize scope that builds payment queries from a `PaymentWithAllFilters` object, with optional order joins.

_Part of [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md)_

The `WithAll` scope on the Payment model lets you filter payments by id, `idempotencyKey`, status, and amount. You pass it a `PaymentWithAllFilters` object with any combination of these filters, and it builds a Sequelize WHERE clause and field selection. If you also include `bisOrderFilters`, the scope joins the related `BisOrder` record and filters by its attributes too—the join is optional (left outer) by default but can be required (inner) via `bisOrderRequired`. The [Payment data service](payment-dto-service.md) calls this scope internally when you search for payments.

**Look at:** [`PaymentScope` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L29) · [`Payment` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L23)

## Pieces

- PaymentWithAllFilters: the filter object shape: Defines the filters you can pass to the `WithAll` scope—id, `idempotencyKey`, status, amount, attributes (field list), and order-related filters.
- WithAll scope: how it builds the query: Spreads filter values into a WHERE clause, builds an ATTRIBUTES list for field selection, and conditionally adds a scoped join to the related `BisOrder` model.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payment table` | Queried by id, `idempotencyKey`, status, amount; specific fields optionally selected via the attributes parameter |
| database | `BisOrder (related via bisOrderId foreign key)` | Optionally joined when `bisOrderFilters` are provided; join mode is left outer by default (includes payments with no order) or inner if `bisOrderRequired` is true |

## Watch out

- Filter values are spread directly into WHERE clauses; you can pass a single value or an array—Sequelize handles both.
- The orders domain is require()d lazily at the file top to break a circular dependency; never use a static import.
- `BisOrder` join defaults to left outer (includes payments with no order); set `bisOrderRequired`: true for an inner join that excludes them.
- The attributes parameter selects specific payment fields; omit it to fetch all, pass an empty array to select none.
